_readme: FIAT GEAR - parts. 30 bases, one job each, written straight to the LIVE name art/items/<slug>.png ('single': one file, no _NN, no sheet, no _response.json). Each job's size is the base's footprint x 64 px (data.gd SIZE / FOOTPRINTS): the game draws the picture at its own pixels, centred, when it fits the cell.

Run: godot --headless --script res://tools/pixellab_batch_v2.gd ++ --manifest res://tools/pixellab_items_parts_manifest.json   (++ --dry-run to list). A job whose file exists is skipped, so a rerun only does what's missing; one that came out wrong: ++ --only <slug> ++ --force, or delete the file and rerun.
Items.slug(base) is the name: lowercase, runs of anything but a letter or digit become one underscore. The cells load the file if it exists and show text if not, so the pool fills in any order.

ORDER: run long_guns first - it has no style image. Promote three or four of the best and copy them to art/reference/items/ref_01.png .. ref_04.png; every other manifest rides those as style_image with every style option on, rotated, so the whole pool shares the guns' palette and rendering.
If the API refuses a wide aspect (a 5x1 gun is 320x64), regenerate at the same width and twice the height; the loader fits and centres it.
Regenerate these manifests with python3 tools/make_item_manifests.py after any footprint change.
